title: "Recitation": the name
hookLine: the word means recitation: it was spoken before it was written

lines: WORDS SOUND DIFFERENT IN A VOICE.
cards: A parent at bedtime, doing all the voices. A friend reading a message out loud, in a funny accent. Words change when someone says them.
They get a speed, a breath, a face behind them. Now the book at the center of Islam. Its name is easy to say, and its meaning is easy to miss: it isn't a word for something written.
It's a word for something spoken. The next three weeks are about how the Qur'an is built: its parts, its verses, its scribes and its reciters. First, the name itself.

teach.b: The word Qur'an comes from the Arabic root q, r, and a catch in the throat: to read aloud, to recite. Qur'an is recitation, the thing that is recited. You've met this root.

The first word the angel Jibril brought to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in the cave of Hira came from it: iqra'. In Pickthall's words: "Read: In the name of thy Lord who createth." Read and recite are one word in Arabic.
And that first revelation came, Muslims say, to a man who did not read or write.
So from the very beginning, the Qur'an was heard before it was written. The Prophet recited what came to him; companions heard it, repeated it and learned it by heart.
Scribes wrote it down too, on whatever was at hand, but the living copy was in voices.
The hadith collections say that every Ramadan, Jibril went over the Qur'an with the Prophet, recitation for recitation, and in his last year, twice.
The Qur'an even tells him how: "chant the Qur'an in measured measure," in Pickthall's rendering of Surah 73.

That's why a child's Qur'an lesson traditionally begins with listening to a teacher and repeating, not silent reading, and why the prayer, the call to prayer and the nights of Ramadan are full of recitation.
The Qur'an also calls itself kitab, a writing, and Muslims hold both: a book you can hold, and a voice you can hear. But its own name leans toward the voice.
When people say it doesn't feel the same on a silent page, this is part of what they mean. It was made to be said.

how: Muslims learn the Qur'an first by listening and repeating after a teacher, and recite it aloud in prayer, in Ramadan and at home; some say it is fully itself only when it is recited.

o: the revealed law that Muslims live by
recitation: the thing that is read aloud
the name of the city where it was first heard

games.q: the name and its root — tap the pairs.
p: the root: to read aloud, to recite
a writing, another of its names
Jibril went over it with the Prophet

s: the Qur'an was written down before it was recited
it was heard first: recited by the Prophet, repeated by the companions, and written down as well.
read and recite are one word in Arabic
the Qur'an only ever calls itself a book
it calls itself kitab, a writing, and also Qur'an, a recitation.

games.q: you're a child starting Qur'an lessons in Cairo or Karachi. what happens in the first lesson?
o: you're handed a book to read silently.
you listen to the teacher and repeat.
games.why: the traditional first lesson is listen and repeat. the Qur'an was a voice before it was a page, and it's still taught that way.

practice: If you know al-Fatiha, or any short surah from the juz' you walked through, say it now, out loud and slowly, and hear what your voice does with it.

If you're learning, say the one line you know best, even just bismillah, or read a line of anything you love at a speaking pace. Then sit in the quiet after it, with the words still hanging in the room.

wordCard.voice: Qur'an. Recitation: the thing that is recited, from the same root as iqra', read. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: recitation, the thing recited. from the root of iqra', read.
